title: Percent increase or decrease from two values
subtitle: Percentages · 6 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **6 of the official questions in Percentages are this one** — 1 Easy, 4 Medium, 1 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get an old value and a new value, stated directly or read off a table or line graph.
- The question asks what percent the value went up or down by, or what percent the new value is of the old one.
- The answer choices are percents, often including the raw difference and the reversed ratio.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 2) Divide by the ORIGINAL (earlier) value, not the later one.
- 3) If the question asks 'new is what percent of old', just compute new ÷ old × 100 and do not subtract.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: With a table, you can enter the values in a table and compute from the cells, but typing the formula is usually faster.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You divide by the new value instead of the old one, or you report the raw dollar or unit difference as the percent.
Another trap is mixing up 'percent of' with 'percent increase'.
For example, the new value can be 160% OF the old one while the increase is only 60%.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
